newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan surplus rise would re-ignite friction - Rubin.
newsitem.headline: Japan surplus rise would re-ignite friction - Rubin.

text.p: A further rise in Japan's current account surplus would re-ignite trade friction for Japan, U.S. Treasury Secretary Robert Rubin said on Friday.
It was essential, in the view of the United States, that Japan's current not rise significantly, he said.
If it did it would create risks for world economic growth, risks of reigniting trade tensions, and could also feed protectionist sentiment, Rubin told a news conference in Tokyo.

Japan faced a challenge of avoiding a significant rise in its trade surplus and also a challenge to increase access to its market, he said after meetings with Japanese leaders including Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto and Finance Minister Hiroshi Mitsuzuka.
